source_meta.issue links: Relates:outward:MC-128329:Seagrass interferes with village bridge generation
source_meta._title: Naturally-generated seagrass and kelp destroys ice

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition 1.21 in a new single-player world. Use the report-provided seed -953538683905638291. Creative mode and enabled commands are recommended solely to permit deterministic execution of the supplied teleport command; the report does not specify a required game mode.
preconditions: Launch the exact Java Edition 1.21 release rather than a newer release or snapshot.
Use a newly created world so the distant target chunks are generated by Minecraft 1.21 when first loaded.
Set the world seed exactly to -953538683905638291, including the leading minus sign.
Enable commands during world creation. Selecting Creative mode is a practical way to enable commands and avoid survival hazards while loading and examining the target location.
Use the default Overworld dimension and do not pre-generate, edit, replace, or manually modify blocks around the target coordinates.
Allow sufficient time for distant terrain and water features to finish rendering after teleportation.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select or create an installation using the exact Minecraft Java Edition 1.21 release, then start the game with that installation.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen identifies the running version as Java Edition 1.21.

steps.action: From the title screen, select Singleplayer, then select Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The new-world configuration screen is open.

steps.action: Set the game mode to Creative and ensure that commands are allowed. Creative mode is not asserted as necessary by the report; it is used to make the supplied teleport command executable and to keep the setup deterministic.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen shows Creative mode, and commands are enabled.

steps.action: Open the world-generation or World settings section containing the seed field. Enter the report-provided seed exactly, preserving its leading minus sign.
steps.success_cue: The seed field contains exactly -953538683905638291 with no spaces or omitted digits.

steps.action: Create the world. Do not reuse an existing world with this seed, because the target terrain should be generated in the selected affected version.
steps.success_cue: The player has spawned in a newly created world and normal first-person movement is available.

steps.action: Wait at the initial spawn point until the nearby terrain has rendered and player movement responds normally. Do not manually travel toward the distant target coordinates.
steps.success_cue: The initial loading overlay is gone, surrounding terrain is visible, and movement responds without a loading pause.

steps.action: Press the Open Chat control, which is T by default, to open the in-game chat input. The command must be executed in-game by the player, not entered in the launcher or world seed field.
steps.success_cue: A chat input field is visible at the bottom of the game screen.

steps.action: Type or paste the report's teleport command exactly as written, including the leading slash. Do not round the coordinates or camera rotation values. The command explicitly places the player in the Overworld at X 22428.278, Y 63, Z -1640.890, with yaw 150.1 and pitch 44.2.
steps.success_cue: The entire command is present in the chat input, ending with the values 150.1 44.2.

steps.action: Press Enter once to execute the teleport command. Do not move the camera or player immediately after executing it; the supplied yaw and pitch are intended to establish the viewing direction at the target location.
steps.success_cue: The player is teleported to approximately X 22428.278, Y 63, Z -1640.890 in the Overworld, and distant target chunks begin loading or are displayed.

steps.action: Wait for the target chunks to finish generating and rendering. Continue only after the terrain, ice, and water around the destination are visible and movement or camera input responds normally. Do not place, break, or replace any blocks while waiting.
steps.success_cue: The terrain at the supplied coordinates is fully rendered, the player remains at the target location, and the camera still faces approximately yaw 150.1 and pitch 44.2.

steps.action: Leave the naturally generated terrain unchanged and hand control to the observation subsystem for inspection of the ice and aquatic vegetation around the commanded viewpoint.
steps.success_cue: The target location is loaded and visible without any player-made block changes that could alter the naturally generated ice, seagrass, or kelp arrangement.

stor.handoff_condition: The fresh Minecraft 1.21 world has generated and loaded the Overworld chunks around X 22428.278, Y 63, Z -1640.890; the player has just arrived using the exact supplied rotation, surrounding terrain is fully rendered, and no blocks at the target location have been modified. Begin observing the naturally generated ice and aquatic vegetation.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a required game mode. Creative mode is recommended only to provide command access and safe, deterministic positioning.

The report does not explicitly state that the target must be visited in a newly created world, but using a fresh world prevents terrain generated or modified by another version from affecting this world-generation reproduction.

The report supplies a teleport viewpoint but does not separately identify an exact individual ice block, seagrass block, or kelp block to target. Observation must therefore begin from the supplied coordinates and camera rotation after the surrounding terrain renders.

The trigger is treated as first loading and generating the distant target chunks when the teleport command is executed; the visible arrangement is already part of the generated terrain by the time loading completes.

source_meta.issue links: Cloners:inward:MC-241277:Server can't generate amplified/large biomes worlds from scratch
source_meta._title: Server doesn't generate amplified / large biome worlds

stor.recommended_version: Minecraft Java Edition 1.16 Pre-release 1 for both the vanilla dedicated server and test client. This is the exact affected version named by the report; do not substitute 1.16 Pre-release 6 or a later release because the report lists Pre-release 6 as the fix version.
stor.environment: A local or remotely accessible vanilla Minecraft Java Edition dedicated server using the official 1.16 Pre-release 1 server JAR, a Java 8-compatible runtime, a fresh writable server directory, and a matching 1.16 Pre-release 1 client. Do not use a modded server, plugin server, proxy, or a world created in singleplayer.
preconditions: The official vanilla dedicated server JAR for Minecraft Java Edition 1.16 Pre-release 1 is available.
The client that will connect to the server is also running Minecraft Java Edition 1.16 Pre-release 1.
Java is installed and can be invoked from a terminal or command prompt with the `java` command.
The tester is authorized to accept the Minecraft EULA by changing `eula=false` to `eula=true`.
Use a new server directory dedicated to this test so that no existing `server.properties`, `level.dat`, or generated world can influence the result.
The server must create the test world from scratch. Do not copy in an amplified world made in singleplayer, an older server world, or any other pre-generated world.
Keep the dedicated server stopped whenever editing `eula.txt`, editing `server.properties`, or removing an accidentally generated world directory.
The test computer has sufficient free memory and disk space to start the server and generate its initial Overworld chunks.
If the client is not running on the same computer as the server, the server address and networking configuration needed to connect are already available.

steps.action: Create a new, empty directory for this reproduction. Place the Minecraft Java Edition 1.16 Pre-release 1 vanilla dedicated server JAR in that directory and rename the JAR to `server.jar` for an unambiguous launch command.
steps.success_cue: The fresh directory contains `server.jar` and does not contain a world directory, `level.dat`, or files copied from another Minecraft world.

steps.action: Open a terminal or command prompt with the fresh server directory as its working directory. Start the server once so that it creates its initial configuration and EULA files. Type the command exactly as shown and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The server reports that the EULA must be accepted, then stops or remains unavailable for normal world startup. `eula.txt` and `server.properties` are present in the server directory.

steps.action: Confirm that the server process from the initial launch is no longer running before editing its files. If it did not terminate automatically, close it only after it has produced `eula.txt` and `server.properties`.
steps.success_cue: No server process is actively writing to the reproduction directory, and both `eula.txt` and `server.properties` are available for editing.

steps.action: Open `eula.txt` in a plain-text editor. After confirming that accepting the EULA is authorized, replace the existing `eula=false` line with the exact line shown, save the file, and close the editor.
steps.success_cue: The saved `eula.txt` contains `eula=true`.

steps.action: Open `server.properties` in a plain-text editor. Locate the property whose line starts with `level-type=`. Replace that entire line with the exact lower-case setting supplied by the report. Do not use a singleplayer world-generation menu and do not add spaces around the equals sign.
steps.success_cue: The saved `server.properties` file contains exactly one active `level-type=amplified` line.

steps.action: In the same `server.properties` file, locate the `level-name=` property and record its value. If it has not been deliberately changed, its value will normally be `world`. Do not otherwise change this property.
steps.success_cue: The executor knows the exact directory name the server will use for the new world, based on the current `level-name` value.

steps.action: While the server remains stopped, inspect the server directory for a folder whose name exactly matches the recorded `level-name` value. If such a folder was accidentally created during an earlier attempt, move it completely outside the server directory or delete it. Also remove matching dimension folders such as `<level-name>_nether` or `<level-name>_the_end` if they exist. Do not reuse or copy any existing world for this test.
steps.success_cue: No folder matching the configured `level-name`, and no associated Nether or End world folder, exists in the server directory. The next startup must therefore create the world from scratch.

steps.action: Close the text editor after saving `server.properties`. Reopen the file once, verify that `level-type=amplified` is still present, then close it without further changes.
steps.success_cue: The server is stopped, the target world directory is absent, and the persisted configuration still contains `level-type=amplified`.

steps.action: From the terminal or command prompt whose working directory is the server directory, start the 1.16 Pre-release 1 dedicated server using the same launch command. Press Enter once after typing it. This startup is the action that causes the dedicated server to create the test world from scratch.
steps.success_cue: The server process remains running and begins preparing or generating a new world under the configured `level-name`.

steps.action: Do not connect a client or interrupt the process while initial world generation is underway. Wait until the server console reports that startup is complete, typically with a `Done` message, and the console is ready to accept input.
steps.success_cue: Initial world generation has completed, the server console is responsive, and the server remains running.

steps.action: Launch the Minecraft Java Edition client using the exact matching version, 1.16 Pre-release 1. From the title screen, select `Multiplayer`. Acknowledge any multiplayer warning screen if it appears.
steps.success_cue: The 1.16 Pre-release 1 client is displaying the Multiplayer server list.

steps.action: Select `Direct Connection`. If the server is running on the same computer as the client, enter `localhost`; otherwise enter the provided server IP address or hostname, including a non-default port if required. Select `Join Server`.
steps.success_cue: The client begins connecting to the dedicated 1.16 Pre-release 1 server and proceeds past the login/loading screens.

steps.action: Wait until the player has spawned in the server's Overworld. Do not begin inspecting the world while the loading screen is visible or while nearby terrain is still appearing. Continue only after surrounding chunks are rendered and player look and movement controls respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the newly generated dedicated-server Overworld, nearby terrain is rendered, movement is responsive, and the server console remains running.

stor.handoff_condition: The 1.16 Pre-release 1 dedicated server has just created a completely new world from scratch with `level-type=amplified` configured, and a matching client is now present in the fully loaded Overworld. Begin observation of the generated world type without replacing, converting, or regenerating the world.
uncertainties: The report does not provide a world seed or spawn coordinates. The server will therefore use an unspecified seed, and the amount of terrain needed for visual classification may vary.

The issue title and comments also identify `largebiomes` as affected, but the report's formal reproduction steps explicitly use `amplified`. This plan uses the report's primary `amplified` case rather than introducing an additional variant.

The original phrase `latest pre-release server .jar` referred to the pre-release current when the report was created. The issue metadata identifies Minecraft Java Edition 1.16 Pre-release 1 as the affected version, so this plan resolves that relative wording to the exact affected version.

The report notes that the server converts capitalization variants such as `AMPLIFIED` or `Amplified` to lower case during startup. The plan writes `amplified` directly and does not make `server.properties` read-only, because the report states that the read-only workaround did not solve the issue.

No exact server JAR filename is supplied in the report. Renaming it to `server.jar` and using the specified Java launch command are practical execution choices and do not change the server version or world-generation configuration.

The report does not specify whether the server and client run on the same machine. The direct-connection step uses `localhost` only for a local server; a remote setup must substitute its actual address.

source_meta.issue links: Duplicate:inward:MC-237671:Liquids in aquifers occasionally do not flow correctly | Duplicate:inward:MC-237688:Weird water generation | Relates:outward:MC-203712:Amethyst Geodes cause floating water/lava to generate when intersecting water/lava caves/pools
source_meta._title: Some water in caves will not start flowing

stor.environment: A newly created single-player Java Edition world in Minecraft 1.18 Pre-release 1, using the Default world type and seed 5518843328198964868. Commands must be available. Creative mode is recommended as a practical execution choice so the player can safely teleport underground and remain stationary without survival-related interference.
preconditions: Launch exactly Minecraft Java Edition 1.18 Pre-release 1, not 1.18 Pre-release 3 or a later release.
Create a new world rather than reusing a world generated in another Minecraft version.
Ensure commands are available. Selecting Creative mode during world creation is the simplest way to satisfy this requirement in single-player.
Use seed 5518843328198964868 and leave the world type set to Default.

After teleporting, do not place or break blocks, empty or collect water, activate pistons, or otherwise interact with blocks near the target water; the report states that a block update can change the water state.
The report does not require a dedicated server, multiple players, a datapack, a resource pack, or a particular graphics setting.

steps.action: From the Minecraft title screen, open the single-player world list by selecting Singleplayer.
steps.success_cue: The Select World screen is open.

steps.action: Start creating a new world by selecting Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is open.

steps.action: Set the game mode to Creative. This is not specified by the report, but it enables commands and prevents underground teleportation from introducing survival hazards.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen displays Creative as the selected game mode, and commands are enabled.

steps.action: Open the additional world-generation settings by selecting More World Options.
steps.success_cue: The seed field and World Type setting are visible.

steps.action: Select the seed input field, remove any existing text, and enter the seed supplied for the 1.18 Pre-release 1 reproduction.
steps.success_cue: The seed field contains exactly 5518843328198964868, with no spaces or extra characters.

steps.action: Verify that World Type is set to Default. If another world type is displayed, cycle the World Type button until it reads Default. Leave all other world-generation options at their normal defaults.
steps.success_cue: The world-generation screen displays World Type: Default.

steps.action: Select Create New World to generate the world from the configured seed.
steps.success_cue: World generation begins and the player eventually appears in the newly created world.

steps.action: Wait at the initial spawn point until world loading is complete enough for commands to respond normally. Do not begin the teleport while the loading screen is still displayed.
steps.success_cue: The loading screen has closed, the world is rendered around the player, and ordinary player or camera input responds normally.

steps.action: Open in-game chat using the Open Chat control; the default Java Edition key is T.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is visible at the bottom of the screen.

steps.action: Enter the report's teleport command exactly as written, including the leading slash, decimal coordinates, yaw, and pitch. Do not replace or normalize any of its arguments.
steps.success_cue: The complete command is visible in the chat input field and has not been altered.

steps.action: Press Enter once to execute the command. This teleports the player within the Overworld to X -3256.64, Y 20.73, Z -5797.15 and applies the report-provided viewing direction.
steps.success_cue: The chat field closes and the player is teleported to an underground cave at the supplied coordinates.

steps.action: Release movement and mouse controls, then wait for the destination chunks and cave geometry to finish rendering. Keep the report-provided camera direction, and do not touch, place, or break blocks near the exposed cave water.
steps.success_cue: The destination cave is fully rendered, movement and rendering are responsive, exposed cave water is visible from or near the arrival view, and no nearby block interaction has occurred since teleportation.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just teleported to X -3256.64, Y 20.73, Z -5797.15 in the Overworld of the seed 5518843328198964868 world. The destination cave and its exposed water have finished rendering, the report-provided viewing direction has been preserved, and no block update or water interaction has been performed. Hand control to the observation subsystem now.
uncertainties: The issue metadata lists 1.18 Pre-release 1 as a fix version, but the later report comment explicitly states that the issue was reproducible in 1.18 Pre-release 1 with seed 5518843328198964868 and the supplied teleport command. This plan preserves that later, version-specific reproduction.
The report does not specify a game mode. Creative mode is a practical execution choice rather than a reported requirement.

The unavailable image and video attachments may identify the precise shape or portion of water to inspect. In their absence, the command's supplied yaw and pitch are preserved so the player arrives facing the reporter's intended view.

The original seed 4876135133240268742 was reported as temporarily non-reproducible in an earlier snapshot. This plan therefore uses the later seed and coordinates supplied specifically for 1.18 Pre-release 1.

source_meta.issue links: Duplicate:inward:MC-239767:One block tall pointed dripstone generates excessively
source_meta._title: Clusters of dripstone (stalagmites) tend to generate abnormally frequent with thickness "tip" on tall caves

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft: Java Edition singleplayer world created and explored entirely in 1.18 Pre-release 4; world type set to Single Biome with the Dripstone Caves biome; commands enabled; player switched to Spectator mode for underground exploration.
preconditions: Install or configure a Minecraft Launcher installation for the exact affected version Minecraft: Java Edition 1.18 Pre-release 4. Do not use 1.18 Pre-release 5 or a later version for this reproduction.
Create a new world in the affected version rather than opening terrain generated by another Minecraft version.
Commands must be enabled so the player can execute the Spectator-mode command.
No world seed or target coordinates are supplied by the report; the cave search therefore takes place in a newly generated random world.
Keep the target terrain naturally generated and unmodified. Do not place, break, or replace pointed dripstone in the cave being inspected.

steps.action: Launch the Minecraft Launcher installation configured for Minecraft: Java Edition 1.18 Pre-release 4 and wait for the main menu to appear.
steps.success_cue: The lower-left portion of the Minecraft main menu identifies the running version as 1.18 Pre-release 4.

steps.action: From the main menu, select Singleplayer, then select Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen is open.

steps.action: Set Game Mode to Creative. Creative is used only as a convenient starting mode before switching to the report-required Spectator mode.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen shows Game Mode: Creative.

steps.action: Open More World Options and set Allow Cheats to ON so that the in-game gamemode command can be executed.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen shows Allow Cheats: ON.

steps.action: Repeatedly select the World Type button until its value is Single Biome. Selecting Single Biome should make a Customize button available. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3AMenu_screen/Java_Edition?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: World Type reads Single Biome and the Customize button is visible.

steps.action: Select Customize to open the biome-selection screen.
steps.success_cue: A screen containing a selectable list of biomes is open.

steps.action: Find and select Dripstone Caves in the biome list. Be careful to select the cave biome named Dripstone Caves rather than a similarly named block or world preset.
steps.success_cue: Dripstone Caves is highlighted as the selected biome.

steps.action: Select Done to confirm the Dripstone Caves biome and return to the world-creation options.
steps.success_cue: The biome-selection screen closes and the new-world configuration remains set to Single Biome.

steps.action: Because the report supplies no seed, leave the seed field empty, then select Create New World.
steps.success_cue: World generation begins and the player eventually appears in the newly created world.

steps.action: Do not begin exploring immediately. Wait until nearby terrain has rendered, the loading overlay is gone, and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The surface around the player is rendered and movement responds without initial world-loading pauses.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Type the Spectator-mode command exactly as supplied in exact_input, including the leading slash, and press Enter. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Minecraft_Wiki%3AProjects/Indonesian_translation/Mode_Penonton?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The command succeeds and the player is switched to Spectator mode.

steps.action: Confirm Spectator movement by briefly pressing Space to fly upward and Left Shift, the default descend control, to fly downward. Release both controls after confirming vertical movement.
steps.success_cue: The player remains airborne and can move vertically without standing on a block.

steps.action: Aim the camera downward and hold the descend control, Left Shift by default, to pass through the surface and enter the underground. Use W to move forward, the mouse to steer, and Space if ascent is needed.
steps.success_cue: The player is below the surface and can pass through solid terrain while searching for open cave spaces.

steps.action: Explore horizontally through underground terrain in Spectator mode. Continue into previously unexplored areas rather than circling only beneath the spawn point. Pause whenever new terrain is rendering so chunk generation can finish before proceeding.
steps.success_cue: New underground terrain renders around the player and movement becomes responsive after each loading pause.

steps.action: Continue the search until a big or tall noise cave is revealed. For this reproduction, identify the target as a broad, naturally generated open cavern with a floor and ceiling separated by a clearly substantial vertical distance; do not use a narrow tunnel, a small enclosed cave, or a player-made excavation. If only small caves are found, continue exploring new terrain in the same world.
steps.success_cue: A broad, vertically tall natural cave is visible, with enough open space to view a sizeable portion of its floor.

steps.action: Move into viewing range of an unexplored or newly rendered section of that large cave until the floor, ceiling, and naturally generated dripstone features have finished generating and rendering. Do not alter any blocks.
steps.success_cue: The selected large-cave section is fully rendered, naturally generated floor stalagmite clusters are visible, and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Release all movement controls and position the camera so that several naturally generated stalagmite clusters across the cave floor can be inspected together. Include as much of the cave's vertical space and ceiling as practical, but do not require the absence of stalactites above the clusters.
steps.success_cue: The camera is stationary and frames multiple natural stalagmite clusters on the floor of the loaded large/tall cave.

stor.handoff_condition: A newly explored section of a naturally generated large/tall noise cave in the Single Biome Dripstone Caves world has just finished loading. The player is stationary in Spectator mode, the terrain remains unmodified, and the camera is positioned to inspect multiple floor stalagmite clusters. Hand control to the observation subsystem now.
uncertainties: The report provides no deterministic seed, coordinates, or cave location, so the amount and direction of exploration cannot be predetermined.

The report does not define a numerical minimum height or volume for a 'big' or 'tall' noise cave. The plan therefore uses a broad open cavern with clearly substantial floor-to-ceiling separation and rejects small caves and narrow tunnels.

The report describes the generation pattern as frequent rather than universal. More than one large cave may need to be loaded and presented to the observation subsystem, but each candidate should be inspected after a single normal loading pass rather than modifying the terrain or repeatedly forcing chunk reloads.

The reporter speculates that affected floor clusters may lack stalactites above them within a noticeable range, but explicitly states that this may be wrong. Absence of overhead stalactites is therefore not treated as a reproduction precondition.
The report offers surface inspection as an alternative route, but this plan uses the primary large-noise-cave route because it most directly matches the stated setup and title.

source_meta.issue links: Relates:inward:MC-240271:Dripstone Cave decorators are different each time ignoring world seed | Relates:inward:MC-219200:Lush Cave decorator is different each time ignoring the world seed
source_meta._title: Decorators are independent of world seed

stor.recommended_version: Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 21w42a, the latest affected snapshot explicitly confirmed in the supplied report. Do not run the primary reproduction in 21w43a, which is listed as the fix version.
stor.environment: Unmodified Minecraft Java Edition 21w42a in single-player, using two newly generated Creative-mode worlds with identical world-generation settings and the exact seed -8718622960759467126. No custom datapacks, mods, or pre-generated world files should be used.
preconditions: Install or create a Minecraft Launcher installation for Java Edition snapshot 21w42a. Snapshot versions must be enabled in the launcher's installation/version settings if 21w42a is not selectable.
Use a clean, unmodified 21w42a client. Using no custom world-generation datapacks is a practical control to ensure that both worlds use the snapshot's built-in generator.
Prepare to retain two separate worlds named MC-238073-A and MC-238073-B; do not delete, recreate, optimize, or convert World A after recording its reference location.
Use the exact signed decimal seed -8718622960759467126 in both worlds.
Use identical world-generation options in both worlds. Only the world names should differ.
Creative mode and commands are enabled as practical execution aids for flying to a clear viewpoint and returning to its exact coordinates; they are not stated as requirements by the report.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select the installation that runs Java Edition snapshot 21w42a.
steps.success_cue: The selected launcher installation displays version 21w42a.

steps.action: Launch the selected installation and wait for the Minecraft main menu to finish loading.
steps.success_cue: The main menu is responsive and identifies the running version as 21w42a.

steps.action: Open the single-player world list.
steps.success_cue: The Select World screen is visible.

steps.action: Begin creating the first fresh comparison world.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is open.

steps.action: Set the first world's name so it can be distinguished from the second world.
steps.success_cue: The World Name field contains MC-238073-A.

steps.action: Set Game Mode to Creative. If the mode selector currently shows another mode, activate it until Creative is displayed.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen displays Game Mode: Creative.

steps.action: Ensure commands are allowed in World A. If necessary, set Allow Cheats to ON.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen displays Allow Cheats: ON.

steps.action: Open the additional world-generation settings containing the seed field.
steps.success_cue: The Seed for the World Generator field and world-generation options are visible.

steps.action: Enter the report's exact seed into the seed field, including the leading minus sign and with no spaces.
steps.success_cue: The seed field contains exactly -8718622960759467126.

steps.action: Leave the generator on the normal built-in configuration: World Type set to Default, Generate Structures enabled, Bonus Chest disabled, and no custom world-generation datapack selected. Record these settings so the same values can be used for World B.
steps.exact_input: World Type: Default; Generate Structures: ON; Bonus Chest: OFF; no custom datapack
steps.success_cue: World A is configured with the exact seed and the recorded default generation settings.

steps.action: Create World A.
steps.success_cue: The world-generation loading screen appears.

steps.action: Wait until World A opens, nearby terrain has rendered, the loading overlay is gone, and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player can move normally in World A and the surrounding spawn-area chunks are visibly rendered.

steps.action: Confirm the loaded world's seed. Press T to open chat, type the command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat reports the world seed as -8718622960759467126.

steps.action: Choose a reference view in the generated area near spawn where naturally generated decorative features are clearly visible. Prefer an outdoor view containing several generated features rather than a close-up of a single block. To obtain a clear overview in Creative mode, double-tap Space to begin flying, use Space to rise, Left Shift to descend, and W/A/S/D to position the player. Remain near the already loaded spawn area rather than exploring randomly for a distant site.
steps.exact_input: Double-tap Space; then use Space, Left Shift, and W/A/S/D
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary at a clear, unobstructed reference viewpoint overlooking generated terrain near spawn.

steps.action: Open the debug overlay with F3. Record the full player position from the XYZ line, including decimals, and the horizontal and vertical viewing angles shown by the Facing line. Label the recorded values X_A, Y_A, Z_A, YAW_A, and PITCH_A.
steps.success_cue: The debug overlay is visible and the exact XYZ position plus yaw and pitch have been recorded for later reuse.

steps.action: While remaining motionless at the reference viewpoint with the debug overlay visible, take a reference screenshot using the screenshot control.
steps.success_cue: Minecraft confirms that a screenshot was saved; the image records World A's reference view and coordinate information.
